Meeting and Attendance
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, November 18, 2025, held at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Also present were Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts and Zendler; Superintendent Machesky; and administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Montante, Pagel, Recker, Milanov, Pawlus, Crowe and Trudel. Approximately 30 members of the audience attended. The meeting adjourned at 9:08 p.m. Minutes submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary. Reference line EA/jh.

Recognitions
Wass Elementary School was honored for its designation as a National Blue-Ribbon School. Because the U.S. Department of Education discontinued the national program, the State of Michigan took over recognizing 2025 Blue Ribbon Schools; Wass was one of 13 public schools in Michigan named. Interim State Superintendent Dr. Sue C. Carnell and State Board President Dr. Pamela Pugh were quoted. Wass was recognized at a Lansing ceremony on November 13; Principal Kristin Crowe and staff came forward. The Communications Department was recognized for 17 National School and Public Relations Association (NSPRA) awards and 5 Michigan School and Public Relations Association (MSPRA) awards. Melissa Verduyn, Thomas Butcher, Adam Burns and Alison Hendry were thanked.

Consent Agenda
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic, to approve items A through D: minutes of the October 7, 2025 Board Workshop; minutes of the October 14, 2025 Board Meeting; Treasurer's Report for September 2025; and a garage door purchase for Troy High School. Yes 7, No 0. Additions and deletions, agenda-item public communication, personnel items, and other business were all recorded as None.

Curriculum
Assistant Superintendent of Elementary Instruction Kris Griffor and Assistant Superintendent of Secondary Instruction Christine DiPilato reported on state assessment performance over time, district-by-district comparisons and gaps between student groups, covering M-STEP, PSAT and SAT results in math, ELA, science and social studies, plus Seal of Biliteracy and AP enrollment and performance. Dr. Recker, Director of Teaching and Learning, previewed the District's new Data Dashboard.

Bond Detail
The $555,000,000 bond issue was passed by voters on November 8, 2022. The District proposed issuing the second series under that proposal in an amount not to exceed $193,000,000 and refunding the 2016 School Building and Site Bonds in an amount not to exceed $27,000,000, combined into a single series not to exceed $220,000,000 to reduce issuance and administration cost. Dr. Richard Machesky and Dan Trudel were authorized to accept a purchase offer.

Other

Student representatives reporting were Chloe Gentilini (Troy College and Career High School), Ahyoung Song (International Academy-East), Sara Graunstadt (Athens High School) and Bella Doss (Troy High School). Dr. Philippart announced the next Board Workshop for December 9 at 6:00 p.m. and the next regular meeting for December 16 at 7:00 p.m., both at the Services Building.

RECOGNITION - NATIONAL BLUE-RIBBON AWARD, WASS ELEMENTARY SCHOOL. The Board recognized Wass Elementary School for its designation as a National Blue-Ribbon School, an award honoring the school as one of the very best in the United States. The minutes note that the U.S. Department of Education discontinued the national program, and that the State of Michigan therefore took over recognizing and designating 2025 Blue Ribbon Schools for exemplary high performance under the federal program. Wass was identified as one of 13 public schools in Michigan to receive the designation. Interim State Superintendent Dr. Sue C. State Board President Dr. Pamela Pugh was quoted saying MDE and the State Board of Education want to ensure these outstanding schools get the recognition they deserve. Wass was recognized by the Interim State Superintendent at a ceremony in Lansing on November 13. Principal Kristin Crowe and several Wass staff members came forward to receive congratulations from the Board.

RECOGNITION - MSPRA AND NSPRA AWARDS. The Board recognized the Troy School District Communications Department, which received 17 National School and Public Relations Association (NSPRA) awards and 5 Michigan School and Public Relations Association (MSPRA) awards. Melissa Verduyn, Thomas Butcher, Adam Burns and Alison Hendry were personally thanked for their service to OneTroy. The 17 national NSPRA awards comprised 6 Awards of Excellence, 6 Awards of Merit and 5 Honorable Mentions. Awards of Excellence: Financial Publication for the TSD 2024 Millage Renewal Guide; Marketing Materials for the 2025 IAE Postcard and the 2025 TSD Pre-K and K Info Night Booklet; Podcast for Attending IAE-The Best is Yet to Come; Special Purpose Publication for the 2025 MLK Day of Service Social Media Ad; and Video Series for Portraits. Honorable Mentions: Magazine for the OneTroy Voice Fall and Winter 2024 Issue; Photo for Alumnus Returns, A Full Circle Moment; and Video-Single entries Making Connections and Celebrating Community, Middle School Collaboration in the TSD, and Authentic Research with Bug Bacteria. The 5 MSPRA Michigan awards were an Award of Excellence for Marketing Materials (Athens High School Profile) and Awards of Merit for Video Series (TSD Alumni Profiles), Podcast (Smith Construction Update, June 2025), Photo (Athens Champion Powerlifting Team) and Infographic (Leonard Elementary Goals). 2025_062_ap_spanish_french.paragraph: Presentation to the Troy Board of Education workshop of December 9, 2025 recommending adoption of new AP Spanish and AP French resources from Vista Higher Learning. The current materials, Abriendo Paso (2014) for AP Spanish and T'es Branche (2014) for AP French, were adopted in 2017, lack current cultural content and AP test preparation, and in the French case are a Level 4 textbook rather than an AP text. Vista was selected over Wayside and Klett because its rigor matches the AP exam, its authors are College Board trainers, and it holds 80 percent of the AP World Languages market share.
2025_062_ap_spanish_french.page:
Purpose
AP Spanish and AP French resource adoption, presented at the 12/9/25 Board Workshop of the Troy School District.

Context and Rationale
The World Language sequence runs Level 1 through Level 5 AP, and the AP exams are written at the intermediate high and advanced levels. The TSD World Languages vision describes learners who can communicate in an ever-expanding global community, discover and experience the heritage of another culture, become resilient risk-takers able to adapt to new environments, improve memory and problem-solving skills, enhance college applications and professional marketability, and open themselves to world travel. AP World Language and Culture is described as equivalent to an intermediate-level college course, in which students apply interpersonal, interpretive and presentational modes of communication while exploring family and communities, personal and public identities, beauty and aesthetics, science and technology, contemporary life, and global challenges. The exam assesses both language and culture, but the resources adopted in 2017 do not represent current culture.

Current State
World Languages operates on a 7-year adoption cycle. Under the PLC structure, Troy AP World Language teachers want a common resource to build cohesion among programs. Current resources are Abriendo Paso (2014) for AP Spanish, with outdated readings that are not updated, no interpersonal speaking practice and no AP test prep; and T'es Branche (2014) for AP French, which is a Level 4 textbook with outdated readings and listening resources. Teachers currently pull materials from a wide variety of sources, some at their own cost.

Selection Process
Guided by Jen Howe, Oakland Schools Heritage and World Language Consultant. Timeline: exploration of resources during the 24-25 school year; 8/11 leadership planning; 8/20 department kickoff and visioning; 10/2 and 10/7 rubric creation and vendor presentations; 10/20 pilot planning; 11/11 and 11/18 PLC planning and check-ins; 12/2 pilot feedback and synthesis.

Vendors Considered
| Vendor | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Wayside | French and Spanish; relatable content with a variety of authentic resources, but does not represent the rigor of the AP assessment and is only a textbook without assessment practice |
| Klett | No AP resource for French; Spanish has many authentic resources and AP practice but does not represent AP rigor, has fewer resources than Vista, and less user-friendly technology |
| Vista Higher Learning | French and Spanish; matches the rigor of the AP exam, culturally relevant resources and a large resource bank; resources may need scaffolding at the start of the year |

Recommended Resource
Vista Higher Learning. Its authors are also College Board trainers, and Vista holds 80 percent of the AP World Languages market share. The 26-27 AP exam will be updated; Vista agreed to provide an updated crosswalk for launching the 26-27 school year and, when it updates its textbooks, to provide updated electronic and physical resources free of cost. The district will bank its professional learning credit to support the change in August. Sample features shown included AP French culturally relevant resources with student supports, an AP Spanish cultural comparison in which a student named Maya contrasts the role of grandparents in the United States and El Salvador, and AP Spanish simulated conversations, a free response task; interpersonal communication practice supports the Free Response AP tasks, which are 50 percent of the exam.

Stakeholder Support and Timeline
Student quotations praised the online textbook for offering more listening and speaking resources, easier navigation, iPad access and speaking practice that built confidence for the heavily weighted speaking sections of the AP test. Student and caretaker surveys were referenced, followed by a financial request slide. Anticipated timeline: December, order placed; January, physical materials inventoried and pilot licenses extended into June; August, 7-year licenses begin and are rostered, with PD from Vista covering College Board changes.
2025_062_ap_spanish_french.verbose:
Board workshop presentation titled AP Spanish and AP French Resource Adoption, delivered at the 12/9/25 Troy School District Board Workshop, proposing replacement of the district's AP world language instructional materials.

CONTEXT AND RATIONALE. The presentation situates AP within the district's world language sequence of Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, Level 4 and Level 5 AP, noting that the AP exams are written at the intermediate high and advanced levels. The TSD World Languages vision states that world language learners can communicate in an ever-expanding global community; discover and experience the rich heritage of another culture; become resilient risk-takers with a greater capacity to adapt to new environments; improve their memory and problem-solving skills for better overall academic performance; enhance their college applications and increase their professional marketability; and open themselves to opportunities for world travel. The AP World Languages vision is quoted as describing AP World Language and Culture as equivalent to an intermediate-level college course in which students cultivate their understanding of language and culture by applying interpersonal, interpretive and presentational modes of communication in real-life situations while exploring concepts related to family and communities, personal and public identities, beauty and aesthetics, science and technology, contemporary life, and global challenges. The presentation stresses that the exam assesses both language and culture, but that the resources adopted in 2017 do not have current culture represented.

CURRENT STATE. World Languages follows a 7-year adoption cycle. With the PLC structure in place, Troy AP World Language teachers desire a common resource to help build cohesion among programs. The current resources are Abriendo Paso (2014) for AP Spanish, criticized for outdated readings that have not been updated, no interpersonal speaking practice and no AP test prep; and T'es Branche (2014) for AP French, which is identified as a Level 4 textbook with outdated readings and listening resources that have not been updated. The stated current reality is that teachers are doing their best to pull resources from a wide variety of sources, some even at their own cost.

PROCESS OF RESOURCE SELECTION. Jen Howe, Oakland Schools Heritage and World Language Consultant, supported the process. The AP resources timeline was: 24-25 school year, exploration of resources; 8/11, leadership planning; 8/20, department kickoff and visioning; 10/2 and 10/7, rubric creation and vendor presentations; 10/20, pilot planning; 11/11 and 11/18, PLC planning and check-ins; and 12/2, pilot feedback and synthesis.

AP VENDORS CONSIDERED, PROS AND CONS. Wayside was evaluated for both French and Spanish; while the resource has relatable content for students with a variety of authentic resources, it does not represent the rigor of the AP assessment and is only a textbook without assessment practice. Klett has no AP resource for French; for Spanish, while the resource has many authentic resources and AP practice, it does not represent the rigor of the AP assessment, does not have the number of resources that Vista has, and its technology was less user friendly. Vista Higher Learning was evaluated for both French and Spanish and was found to match the rigor of the AP exam, providing meaningful, culturally relevant resources as well as a large resource bank; because of that rigor, resources may need to be scaffolded at the start of the year. Additional points favoring Vista: the authors of Vista are also College Board trainers; Vista has 80 percent of the AP World Languages market share; the 26-27 AP exam will be updated and Vista has agreed to provide an updated crosswalk for launching the 26-27 school year; when Vista updates its textbooks it will provide the district updated electronic and physical resources free of cost; and the district will bank its professional learning credit to support this change in August.

FEATURES OF THE RECOMMENDED TEXTS. Illustrative slides covered AP French culturally relevant resources, and AP French culturally relevant resources with student supports. For AP Spanish, a cultural comparison example was shown: on the AP test students must compare the country they are studying with the United States, and in the sample a student named Maya shares how the role of grandparents differs in the United States versus El Salvador. Another example showed AP Spanish simulated conversations, described as a free response task on the AP exam. The presentation notes that this is an example of interpersonal communication that fosters student confidence and practice for the Free Response AP tasks, which constitute 50 percent of the exam.

ADDITIONAL STAKEHOLDER SUPPORT. Two student quotations were included. One student said they like an online textbook because it has more resources such as listening and speaking, they can navigate the pages better and faster, and it is easier to have the textbook on an iPad. A second student said they have used the ebook many times in class and the variety of resources has been really helpful; that the hardest part of learning Spanish at this level is being able to speak their thoughts; that the ebook gave them speaking practice that already allowed them to feel more confident about their speaking abilities; and that the speaking sections of the AP test are huge, very important to the overall score and heavily weighted, so having these resources builds confidence in trying to get a good score. Slides for a Student Survey and a Caretaker Survey followed.

FINANCIAL REQUEST AND TIMELINE. A financial request section was included in the deck. The anticipated timeline moving forward is: December, order placed; January, physical materials inventoried and pilot licenses extended into June; August, 7-year licenses begin and are rostered, with professional development from Vista covering the College Board changes. The presentation closes with a questions slide.

SLIDE 14, CPR AND FIRST AID CERTIFICATION. A mandate started by the MHSAA in 2024-25 requires all head coaches to be CPR and first aid certified, through an online course with an in-person skills test.

SLIDE 15, EAP DRILLS. Two EAP drills per season, described as two CPR/AED drills per season, covering the location of the AED, what the rest of the team should do and where the team should go, with trainers assisting or observing the drill for practice.

SLIDE 16, COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS. The athletic department goal is to provide learning with local community partnerships to coaches, parents and student-athletes. SLIDE 10, MEMORANDUM. Dated Tuesday, December 9, 2025, to the TSD Board of Education, from Christine DiPilato and Kristine Griffor, on Schools of Choice Recommendations for the 2026-2027 School Year. The factors considered were current enrollment across the Troy School District; enrollment projections, patterns and trends; numbers and percentages of Schools of Choice students currently in the district; the projected number of Schools of Choice siblings age-eligible to enter the district in 2026-2027 if the decision is made to admit a limited number of kindergarten, first and sixth through eighth grade students under Schools of Choice; and available elementary classrooms. The recommendations are to use Plante Moran Realpoint enrollment projection numbers as the foundation for determining the number of Schools of Choice students to admit for the 2026-2027 school year, and to accept Schools of Choice applications for kindergarten at 83 under Section 105 and 4 under Section 105C, first grade at 25 under Section 105 and 1 under Section 105C, and sixth to eighth grade combined at 2 under Section 105 and 1 under Section 105c. Based upon the number of applications to kindergarten received for the 2025-2026 school year, administration anticipates attracting many more than 12 sibling preference survey response applicants, which would allow the district to admit 87 kindergarteners. Middle school students would be placed in a building according to available space.
